who: German literature, sound and media scholar at the University of Michigan; PhD Columbia 2013.

evidence.says: Identifies the author of Eardrums as Michigan assistant professor of German, with a Columbia PhD in 2013.
CV records Michigan appointments from 2013 onward and lists Kathryn Wataha (History), with an ultrasound/echolocation dissertation, under Graduate Dissertation Committees.

notes: The CV uses a related dissertation title for Wataha. It establishes committee membership, without specifying chairship.

who: Medieval European historian at the University of Oregon; PhD Notre Dame 1997.

evidence.says: Identifies Lisa Wolverton/Lisa Ann Wolverton; the Reinventing Knowledge citation places her in the University of Oregon history department.
Approval page of Michael Anthony Furtado’s Islands of Castile lists Lisa Wolverton as chairperson; degree awarded September 2011 at Oregon.
Oregon’s 2009–10 catalogue lists Wolverton in medieval Europe, with a Notre Dame PhD in 1997 and a faculty appointment beginning in 2000.

notes: Student, institution, period and Notre Dame doctorate agree.

who: Françoise N. Hamlin, historian of African American history at Brown; PhD Yale 2004.

evidence.says: Identifies Françoise N. Hamlin, author of Crossroads at Clarksdale and associate professor of African Studies and History at Brown University.
Brown identifies Françoise N. Hamlin as associate professor of History and Africana Studies, with a Yale PhD in 2004, and lists the same books; profile includes a Brown advising award in 2026.

notes: Institution, Yale doctorate and authored works agree. The individual El-Shabazz advising relationship was not independently located.

who: Early modern French historian at the University of Ottawa, specializing in family and legal history.

evidence.says: Cites Ottawa’s faculty profile for Sylvie Perrier, specialist in early modern French history, family and legal history, and author of Des enfances protégées.
The indexed Ottawa thesis approval page for Samy Khalid’s Les Suisses, révélateurs de l’imaginaire national canadien names Sylvie Perrier as thesis co-supervisor and Chad Gaffield as supervisor.

notes: The repository’s indexed approval page directly connects Perrier to Khalid; full PDF retrieval was unavailable.

who: Marcela Kličova Perett, medieval historian at North Dakota State; PhD Notre Dame 2009.

evidence.says: Equates Marcela Kličova Perett and Marcela K. Perett, author of Preachers, Partisans, and Rebellious Religion; records Notre Dame PhD, Medieval Studies, 2009.
NDSU’s 2023–24 history catalogue lists Marcela Perett as graduate program director, with a Notre Dame Medieval Institute PhD in 2009.
Spring 2023 commencement program lists Carol A. Bentley’s history dissertation An Affront to Common Decency: Censoring Film in the US and Great Britain, with advisor Dr. Marcela Perett.

notes: Exact student and dissertation match, supported by the matching institution and doctorate.

who: Constance B. Hilliard, African historian at the University of North Texas; PhD Harvard 1977.

evidence.says: Identifies Constance B. Hilliard, author of The Intellectual Traditions of Pre-Colonial Africa; its 1997 citation names the University of North Texas.
UNT identifies Constance B. Hilliard as a history professor and records a Harvard history PhD in 1977, with a dissertation on Senegalese historiography.

notes: Name, UNT appointment and Harvard doctorate agree. Stillwell’s individual advising relationship was not independently verified.

who: Kathleen D. Morrison, South Asian archaeologist and historical anthropologist at Chicago; PhD Berkeley 1992, later at Penn.

evidence.says: Identifies Kathleen D. Morrison as Chicago professor of Anthropology and Social Sciences, with a Berkeley PhD in 1992, researching South Asian archaeology and historical anthropology.

The indexed publisher preview of Byron Hamann’s Bad Christians, New Spains, acknowledgments p. x, names Kathleen Morrison on his 2011 dissertation committee in Chicago’s History and Anthropology departments.
Penn’s faculty profile identifies Kathleen Morrison as an anthropologist studying South Asian historical ecology and records a Berkeley anthropology PhD in 1992.

notes: The Chicago anthropologist is the matching candidate. Hamann’s acknowledgment establishes committee membership, without specifying chairship.

who: Eugene Y. Park, historian of Korea at the University of Pennsylvania during the relevant period; PhD Harvard 1999.

evidence.says: A January 2018 Stanford University Press citation identifies Eugene Y. Park as Korea Foundation Associate Professor of History at Penn; another citation records a Harvard PhD in East Asian Languages and Civilization, 1999.

The publicly indexed repository dissertation, Agriculture and Development in an Age of Empire: Institutions, Associations, and Market Networks in Korea, 1876–1945, identifies Holly Stephens and Eugene Y. Park on its abstract page.

notes: The dissertation’s indexed abstract and the LC record’s Penn appointment support Eugene Y. Park; full dissertation retrieval was unavailable.
